00024 void normalize( int dim_in, double *vtx_in )
00025 {
00026         int i;

00046 double angle( int dim_in, double *u1_in, double *u2_in, double *v1_in, double *v2_in )
00047 {
00048         int i;

00050         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00051                 u2_in[i] -= u1_in[i], v2_in[i] -= v1_in[i];
00052         normalize( dim_in, u2_in );

00063 void project( int dim_in, double *orig_in, double *norm_in, double *vec_in )
00064 {
00065         int i;
00066         double dp;
00067         vec_sub( dim_in, orig_in, norm_in );
00068         vec_sub( dim_in, orig_in, vec_in );
00069         normalize( dim_in, norm_in );
00070         dp = dotp( dim_in, norm_in, vec_in );
00071         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00072                 norm_in[i] *= dp;
00073 }

00079 void subspace_project( int dim_in, int mdim_in, double *mnfd_in, double *point_in, double *proj_out )
00080 {
00081         int i,j;
00082         double dot,len;
00083 
00084         /* Keep the running total */
00085         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00086                 proj_out[i] = 0.0;
00087 
00088         /* Want point_in relative to mnfd_in[0] */
00089         vec_sub( dim_in, mnfd_in, point_in );
00090         for(i=1;i<mdim_in;i++)
00091                 vec_sub( dim_in, mnfd_in, mnfd_in + i * dim_in );
00092 
00093         /* Now project onto each generalized surface vertex */
00094         for(i=1;i<mdim_in;i++)
00095         {
00096                 len = length( dim_in, mnfd_in + i * dim_in );
00097                 dot = dotp( dim_in, point_in, mnfd_in + i * dim_in ) / len;
00098                 for(j=0;j<dim_in;j++)
00099                         proj_out[j] += dot * mnfd_in[i*dim_in+j] / len;
00100         }
00101         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00102                 proj_out[i] += mnfd_in[i];
00103 }

00110 void rotate_axis( int dim_in, int mdim_in, double *mnfd_in, double *point_in, double angle_in, double *point_out )
00111 {
00112         int i,j;
00113         double n[dim_in],p[dim_in],q[dim_in],dot,len,x,y;
00114 
00115         /* Preserve original vectors */
00116         bcopy( point_in, p, dim_in * sizeof(double) );
00117 
00118         /* Calculate p = r - r proj n */
00119         subspace_project( dim_in, mdim_in, mnfd_in, point_in, n );
00120         vec_sub( dim_in, n, p ); /* p is now a vector pointing away from the manifold toward point_in */
00121         len = length( dim_in, p ); /* len is the radius of point_in from the manifold */
00122         normalize( dim_in, p ); /* Now point_in = n + len * p */
00123 
00124         /* Now do Gramm-Schmidt to orthogonalize relative to mnfd_in and p */
00125         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00126                 q[i] = 1.0; /* Does not matter what vector is used */
00127         for(i=1;i<mdim_in;i++)
00128         {
00129                 normalize( dim_in, mnfd_in + i * dim_in );
00130                 dot = dotp( dim_in, mnfd_in + i * dim_in, q );
00131                 for(j=0;j<dim_in;j++)
00132                         q[j] -= dot * mnfd_in[i*dim_in+j];
00133         }
00134 
00135         /* FIXME: Need to standardize the DIRECTION, i.e. + or -, of q to make input angles correct     */
00136         /* FIXME: Want vectors listed in right-handed order relative to the manifold                    */
00137         dot = dotp( dim_in, p, q );
00138         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00139                 q[i] -= dot * p[i];
00140         assert( length( dim_in, q ) > 0.0 );
00141         normalize( dim_in, q );
00142 
00143         /* Now p (adjacent) and q (opposite) are the vectors which determine the rotation */
00144         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00145                 point_out[i] = 0.0;
00146         x = cos( angle_in );
00147         y = sin( angle_in );
00148         for(i=0;i<dim_in;i++)
00149                 point_out[i] += len * ( x * p[i] - y * q[i] ) + n[i];
00150 }
